title: FFmpeg: fifty-three defects across five boundaries -- thirty-eight past a direct av_malloc, four in a buffer pool, eleven inside one allocation

plain-heap-repros.boundary: the system allocator itself: one av_malloc_array or av_calloc, with no inner layer
plain-heap-repros.title: Upstream FFmpeg spatial defects that cross the MALLOC BOUND, FFmpeg's not-nested row
plain-heap-repros.note: The third plain-heap corpus, after memcached's and wireshark's, and a sibling of subobject-repros and pool-repros rather than part of either: those boundaries are 'inside one allocation' and 'storage an AVBufferPool handed out', while every case here leaves a buffer FFmpeg obtained DIRECTLY from av_malloc_array or av_calloc. Under this inventory's axis (WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT) all four rows are NOT NESTED. ASan REPORTS all four, two-sided, unlike the sub-object corpora -- which is the contrast this corpus exists to draw. Case 2 is the only row in the whole inventory that crosses BELOW an allocation's base. All four are fix-reversals: liveness is recorded, never required, and requiring it is what kept FFmpeg's spatial count at four. WHY THE PLATFORM ALLOCATOR. These cases call the platform's calloc, not the buffer-pool port's av_malloc. That port's av_malloc (ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/src/shared/metadata-allocator.c:26) is a bump/freelist carve out of ONE arena returning a raw interior pointer, and it rounds every request up to 64 bytes; __builtin_capstone_cap_shrink appears only in src/capstone-domain/payload-capabilities.c:57, on pool PAYLOAD blocks. Routing these cases through it would leave no per-allocation bound to cross AND would absorb every small crossing in the round-up, so the reading would be about the arena, not the defect. Triage and the full candidate disposition: docs/ref/ffmpeg-spatial-defect-triage.md. CheriBSD MEASURED 2026-10-06 (results/20261006-cheribsd): 3 of 4 CAUGHT with the fault attributed to the labelled probe, si_code 1; case 1 NOT caught, refuting its pre-registered prediction because its 24-byte request yields a 32-byte capability. This is the first CheriBSD reading of any FFmpeg corpus, and the first in the tree where attribution is established -- the probes are defined once externally rather than static per translation unit.

plain-temporal-repros.boundary: the platform allocator's own bound -- a direct allocation, no inner layer
plain-temporal-repros.title: Lifetime defects on a direct ffmpeg allocation, with no suballocator between it and the platform

plane-repros.boundary: a bound between two PLANES of one AVBuffer, as av_frame_get_buffer carves them
plane-repros.title: Upstream FFmpeg spatial defects that leave a frame PLANE while staying inside the frame's single allocation
plane-repros.note: The third FFmpeg corpus and the one the inventory's nested-spatial cell needed. pool-repros holds storage an AVBufferPool handed out and took back (temporal); subobject-repros holds a bound between two MEMBERS of one av_malloc (spatial, NOT nested, because av_refstruct_alloc_ext is called directly); this one holds a bound between two PLANES of one AVBuffer, which is spatial AND nested. That every plane comes from a single buffer is measured rather than assumed: a YUVA420P frame reports buf[1] == NULL with 1024 bytes of slack after the alpha plane inside that one buffer, so a read leaving the plane stays inside the allocation exactly as a wmem chunk overread stays inside its block. ASan is SILENT here and reports the memcached plain-heap row; the two readings side by side are the project's axis, measured rather than argued. The declared port is the app port rather than buffer-pool: buffer-pool compiles only libavutil/buffer.c and refstruct.c, while this case needs frame.c, imgutils.c and pixdesc.c, so the app port (whole libavutil) is the only one that could host a domain build of it. Today the corpus is native-only.

pool-repros.title: Consumer-side temporal defects whose stale storage an FFmpeg pool handed out

subobject-repros.boundary: sub-object bounds inside ONE allocation (av_refstruct / av_malloc)
subobject-repros.title: Upstream FFmpeg spatial defects that cross a bound INSIDE ONE ALLOCATION -- between two members of a struct, or between two slices carved from one block by arithmetic
subobject-repros.note: A sibling of pool-repros, deliberately separate: that corpus's boundary is storage an AVBufferPool handed out, and these defects cross a bound inside a single allocation, which is a different boundary. The seam is a verbatim copy of pool-repros' -- each corpus owns a private copy, and the FF2_* infrastructure macros come from the port's replay-config. Cases 0-2 are LIVE at the n9.0.1 pin; cases 3-9 were added 2026-10-06, of which 5, 6 are live and 3, 4, 7, 8, 9 are fix-reversals -- liveness is RECORDED, never required, and requiring it is what kept this cell at three cases. Under this inventory's axis (WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT) every row here is NOT NESTED: the object is one allocation and nothing sub-allocated the crossed region. No arm we have catches any of them; the oracle is the upstream fix. The Capstone arms for 3-9 are declared predictions -- cases 0-2 got theirs from probe cases 40-42 of ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/security-tests, which is the seam 3-9 will use. Triage and the full candidate disposition: docs/ref/ffmpeg-spatial-defect-triage.md. CheriBSD MEASURED 2026-10-06 (results/20261006-cheribsd): 0 of 10 caught, 22/22 arms, both platform controls firing -- and the reason is recorded as WEAKER than 'the bound is the allocation', because the port's av_malloc is an un-narrowed arena carve.
